title: CORS: what it is and what it isn't
summary: CORS relaxes the browser's same-origin policy for chosen sites. It is not authentication, and it protects nothing from curl.

steps.title: The same-origin policy, and CORS
body: An **origin** is scheme + host + port: `https://app.example` and `https://api.example` are different origins.

Browsers enforce the **same-origin policy**: script on `https://evil.example` may *send* requests to your API, but it may **not read the responses**. That is what stops a random site from reading your webmail through your logged-in browser.
**CORS** (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) is how your API *relaxes* that rule for origins you trust:
Seeing that header, the browser lets `app.example`'s script read the response.
- **Not authentication or authorization.** `curl`, Postman and servers ignore CORS completely. Every endpoint still needs its own auth.
- **Not CSRF protection by itself.** A simple cross-site form POST is *sent* regardless; CORS only governs reading the answer (and preflights for non-simple requests).
- Something you configure on the **API**, read by the **browser**.

steps.prompt: A team says: "Our API is safe from scrapers because CORS only allows `https://app.example`." Why is that wrong?
options: CORS is enforced by browsers; a script using curl or HttpClient ignores it entirely
CORS headers can be forged by the browser
CORS only applies to GET requests
It is right: CORS blocks all other clients

steps.title: Preflight requests
body: Before a "non-simple" cross-origin request (a `PUT` or `DELETE`, JSON `Content-Type`, an `Authorization` header), the browser first asks permission with a **preflight**:
Only if the answer allows it does the browser send the real request. `Max-Age` lets it cache the answer.

- **Reflecting any `Origin`** back into `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` together with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. Now *every* website can make authenticated requests with your users' cookies and read the results.
- `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on an API that uses cookies (browsers refuse `*` with credentials, so people "fix" it by reflecting, see above).
- Allowing `null` as an origin (sandboxed iframes and local files send it).

steps.prompt: Arrange what happens for a cross-origin `POST` with JSON from `https://app.example`.
lines: the browser sends OPTIONS with Origin and Access-Control-Request-Method
the API answers with the Access-Control-Allow-* headers
the browser checks the origin, method and headers are allowed
the browser sends the real POST
the API's own authentication and authorization run
the browser lets the page's script read the response

steps.prompt: Match each header to who sends it and why.
pairs: browser: where the request comes from
browser, in a preflight: the method it wants to use
server: this origin may read the response
server: how long the preflight answer may be cached

steps.prompt: Which CORS configuration is the most dangerous for an API authenticated by cookies?
options: Echoing any request's `Origin` back with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`
A preflight cache of ten minutes

steps.prompt: Which request does a browser send **without** a preflight?
options: A cross-origin `GET` with no custom headers
steps.explain: "Simple" requests (GET, HEAD, or POST with form content types and no custom headers) go straight out. That's why CORS alone never protects state-changing GETs or form posts.

steps.title: Configure CORS
prompt: Add a CORS policy named `"web"` with the built-in CORS services. **Run checks** starts the server and sends real preflights.
- apply it to the whole app with `app.UseCors("web")`
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await Dojo.TryAsync("Simple requests could be checked", async () =>
DojoWeb.Status("GET from the app's origin still returns 200", 200, ok);
Dojo.Eq("another origin gets no Access-Control-Allow-Origin", null, H(evil, "Access-Control-Allow-Origin"));
await Dojo.TryAsync("Preflights could be checked", async () =>
DojoWeb.Status("a preflight from the app gets 204", 204, pre);
Dojo.Check("allowing Authorization and Content-Type", headers.Contains("authorization") && headers.Contains("content-type"), headers);
var del = await Send(http, HttpMethod.Options, "/api/notes", "https://app.example", "DELETE", null);
var evil = await Send(http, HttpMethod.Options, "/api/notes", "https://evil.example", "POST", null);
Dojo.Eq("a preflight from another origin isn't approved", null, H(evil, "Access-Control-Allow-Origin"));
static string? H(HttpResponseMessage r, string name) =>
r.Headers.TryGetValues(name, out var v) ? string.Join(",", v) : null;
static Task<HttpResponseMessage> Send(HttpClient http, HttpMethod m, string url, string origin, string? reqMethod = null, string? reqHeaders = null)
